faults.quote: The average one-way fare on Hub–Lakeport fell from $200 in FY2023 to $120 in FY2025.
faults.why: The candidate asked for average fare by route, mainly Lakeport and Port Avery. Only Lakeport's fare was released. The case holds Port Avery's fare ($240 to $160), which got no word, and there was no 'I don't have' for the other routes.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: On Hub–Lakeport, revenue fell from $26.4M to $16.8M and contribution fell from $8.4M to a $1.2M loss
faults.why: The full exhibit-1 route lines, already on screen, were repeated as part of the answer to a fare ask they don't answer.

faults.quote: You said Port Avery revenue fell from about $44 million to $32.4 million. Where did the $44 million come from?
faults.why: In t7 the candidate misquoted the interviewer's Lakeport fare as 'about $125' (the line said $120) and used it to get 134,000 passengers. No flat correction came; the interviewer instead probed an older figure.

faults.quote: I don't have avoidable fixed cost by route.
faults.why: The case holds coarse answers: all nine aircraft are leased through 2030 and can't be returned, and fixed costs would not change. So avoidable fixed cost is essentially nil. The fixed-costs-unchanged note did reach the candidate on exhibit-3 two turns later.

faults.quote: Understood. Setting that plan aside, what else could Larkspur do to make sure it's profitable in the first year?
faults.why: The candidate asked to stress-test demand on Ashford and Brookhaven. The case holds new-route ramp-up data (6–12 months, about 60% first-year load factor). The ask got no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: You said roughly 800,000 passengers a year across the network.
faults.why: This flagged a correct figure (about 840,000) as if it needed checking, prompting the candidate to re-verify right math.

faults.quote: What would you do to guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's previous answer had already given a detailed mitigation (market research, staged rollout, phased exits), so this re-asks it.
